predecessors.name: Byeonhan confederacy
predecessors.text: the Nakdong basin of Byeonhan, whose states 'most ... joined' the Gaya confederacy

successors.name: Silla
successors.text: the last Gaya land: Daegaya and the remaining polities of the Nakdong basin

ledger.x: 301: the Gaya confederacy takes over from Byeonhan around Gimhae.
532: Geumgwan Gaya, the ruling state of Gaya, falls to Silla.
562: Daegaya falls and Gaya is gone.

wars.name: Goguryeo's pressure on Gaya
wars.outcome: The Gaya page says the confederacy 'disintegrated under pressure from Goguryeo between 391 and 412', yet the same page has Geumgwan conquered in 532 and Daegaya in 562.

wars.name: Silla's conquest of Gaya
wars.outcome: Silla destroyed Takgitan Gaya in 529, took Geumgwan Gaya in 532 and Daegaya in 562; Gaya ended.

wars.name: Battle of Gwansan Fortress
wars.outcome: Daegaya allied with Baekje against Silla; both sides took heavy losses, Daegaya lost the leadership of Gaya to Ara Gaya and fell eight years later.

certainty.note: A confederacy of city-states in river valleys with no frontier on any page; the Cliopatria outline is a block of the lower Nakdong.
